Well, Tiny Palm was at the Dreamland and this Cliff Jones, we call him Snag, he come up one day to my house and told me that Tiny Palm sent him to get me to play with him. So I went on down and made rehearsal with him and went through okay. So I worked there at the Dreamland with him and then tell the truth, we come on down there and played dances, you know all these. Yeah, middle trip, all the way, you know, tour.
That's the State Street, the Dreamland on State Street.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: I made records with Tiny Palm

ctx.x: He was on, he might have played bass on some of them records I made, I don't know, because I was with him right now. But I'll tell you the band, I made records with me and Al Wynn, then I made records with Francois Luzan, I made records with Jimmy Weed, I made records with Tiny Palm, then I made some of my own, you know, with a bunch I had. Somebody else I made records with, I can't think, no. I made records with a lot of guys.
I was just thinking about Tiny Palm, did you ever play any of his arrangements?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: The only band I sat down and read music with, best I could, was Tiny Pond and Jelly Roll Morton and Huey Swift.

ctx.x: Punch, in 1919, when you first got here, what did the brass bands play like? Were they strictly music? Were they here?

No, they played more marches then. But I'm going to tell you now, I ain't going to lie to you. Hick was a very few men's in them bands reading. Like the trumpet players be reading. But them other guys were just speaking. I mean, you know, using their brains. They could hear a tune and play it. That's right. Yeah. That's right. Now you take men like Joe Howard, and them men that were playing. They had their music up. They were playing it, see? But they had men on trombone, men on alto, and things like that. They…
Well, what about Louie? Did you ever work with him?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Yeah, I made good money with Tiny Palm

ctx.x: Oh yeah, in those days. In Chicago you told me about making real good money with Tiny Palm.

Yeah, I made good money with Tiny Palm and I made my best money with Oliver Bibbs. So Oliver Bibbs, I made the best money with him. I got ninety, eighty-five dollars, Tiny Palm, but I got a hundred dollars flat every week with this Oliver Bibbs.
What about somebody like Francois when you had those five years?
